models.name: Model A: FSI-informed LES
models.what_it_computes: Transient large-eddy simulation of pulsatile flow with prescribed leaflet kinematics; outputs include hinge-region velocity fields, instantaneous shear rate, Lagrangian particle residence time, and washout time constants.

models.name: Model B: Steady RANS with Porous-Hinge Surrogates
models.what_it_computes: Time-averaged Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes with porous-joint representations for sub-gap leakage; outputs include mean hinge through-flow, scalar washout index, and near-wall shear proxies.

models.name: Model C: Lattice–Boltzmann Microscale Hinge CFD
models.what_it_computes: Voxel-resolved hinge recess simulation from micro-CT geometry; computes full Lagrangian residence-time distributions, escape probabilities, and shear exposure metrics during systolic/diastolic phases.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 1: Diastolic leakage-driven washout
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Reverse-pressure leakage jets during valve closure are a primary driver of contaminant and platelet clearance from hinge recesses when bulk forward flow is absent.

mechanisms.name: Mechanism 2: Systolic vortex-pumping washout
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Forward-flow shear layers and hinge-adjacent vortices entrain hinge fluid and promote exchange with the main stream, affecting residence time during peak ejection.

deviation.detail: All credibility factors are scored on a 0–7 integer scale per model–mechanism pair, where 0 indicates no supporting evidence and 7 indicates comprehensive evidence.

expected_decision.outcome_source: For the context of use—demonstrating hinge washout equivalence of a modified geometry to a reference design to reduce benchtop dye-visualization testing—the LES and microscale lattice–Boltzmann models can credibly carry evi-dentiary weight for both mechanisms, with strongest support for diastolic leakage-driven washout.

expected_context_of_use: The decision-maker seeks to determine whether a proposed hinge geometry modification maintains hinge washout perfor-mance equivalent to a reference bileaflet valve design when operated under adult aortic in-vitro conditions.

spans: For Model C, the lattice–Boltzmann implementation was verified using MMS tailored to the D3Q19 TRT formulation, with a divergence-free manufactured velocity field and corre-sponding forcing term.
The observed convergence rate was 1.95 in grid refinement from 8 µm to 2 µm voxel sizes in a periodic domain.
Lid-driven cavity flows at Reynolds numbers 100 and 1000 reproduced benchmark centerline velocity profiles and vortex-center locations within 2% and 0.5 grid spacings, respectively.

The pressure boundary implementation was tested in a one-dimensional acoustic propagation problem to ensure minimal spurious reflections; amplitude decay and phase speed matched analytical predictions within 1%.
findings.span: For Model C, the lattice–Boltzmann implementation was verified using MMS tailored to the D3Q19 TRT formulation, with a divergence-free manufactured velocity field and corre-sponding forcing term.

spans: For Mechanism 2, the recess-mouth interaction with the main stream is represented through pressure-driven interface conditions rather than an explicit upstream flow field.
